subject: Medale — capacity roadmap, cutover window & autoscale guardrails
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: James Park <james.park@medalehealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medale — capacity roadmap, cutover window & autoscale guardrails

Hi James — great to meet last week. Per our kickoff, attaching a concise set of asks so we can finalize the Dedicated activation timetable and technical handoff. High-level ask: pick a preferred 72-hour cutover window in April for the initial pool turnup and one week for post-go-live validation.

Quick summary of what we need from your side before we schedule turnup: 
- Confirm target peak concurrent QPS (sustained and burst) and expected daily patterns (timezone-normalized).
- Approve the autoscale & burst policy thresholds (suggested in the attached spreadsheet).
- Provide an on-call contact for netops and a primary procurement POC for final SOW/MPA sign-off.

Operational items Redwood will deliver prior to cutover: 
- Provisioned GPU pool (4 x A100 80GB equivalent lanes) in us-east-1 with warm-cache priming.
- Canary routing to reduced traffic for first 24 hours + automatic fallback to hosted model variants.
- Preflight simulations (tokenized load replay) and a dry-run on the staging cluster.

Attachments: medale_mpa_draft_v2.pdf (terms), cutover-checklist.xlsx (milestones), pool-provisioning-diagram.png

Proposed next steps: Reply with (1) preferred 72-hour window, (2) any baseline traffic revisions, (3) final procurement contact — we’ll lock dates and schedule a preflight dry-run.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Customer Success 
Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 11 Mar 2029 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medale — capacity roadmap, cutover window & autoscale guardrails

Sofia / team — copying in ops and implementation to scope the provisioning plan. Notes from my side after James’ reply:

1) Capacity sizing: James’ sustained peak ~420 QPS with 1,800 short spikes. We should recommend keeping a 2.5x burst headroom for batch imports (so suggested burst capacity = ~4 x baseline lanes).

2) Warm-cache priming: We’ll run a staged KV warmup where we prepopulate prefixes for the top 200 routes and pin a subset to warm nodes for T+0. Multi-AZ behavior: we’ll provision pool in us-east-1b and us-east-1c with cross-AZ read fallback; we’ll document expected replication lag in the cutover checklist.

3) Canary plan: Day 0 — 10% traffic to dedicated pool; Day 1 — 40% with degradation gates; Day 2 — 100% with 48-hour monitoring window. Auto-fallback to hosted variants at route-level if p50 latency exceeds 250ms or error rate >0.8%.

Action items for Connor/Infra: please prepare the provisioning terraform snippet and a quick smoke test that verifies KV cache hits. Priyom — please draft the runbook sections for the cutover-checklist.xlsx: preflight, dry-run, escalation steps, rollback criteria.

Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medale — capacity roadmap, cutover window & autoscale guardrails

Quick draft of the cutover timeline based on agreed windows (Apr 9–11):

- Apr 7 (EOD): final MPA signoff + procurement confirmation — blocks green.
- Apr 8 (09:00–13:00 ET): Staging dry-run — replay last 72 hours of tokenized traffic, validate performance and cache hit rates.
- Apr 9 (02:00–06:00 ET): Provision GPU pool & network setup; verify security group rules and private endpoints.
- Apr 9 (11:00 ET): Start canary (10% traffic) — monitor SLOs for 6 hours.
- Apr 10 (11:00 ET): Ramp to 40% — validate autoscale triggers with synthetic spikes.
- Apr 11 (11:00 ET): Full cutover to dedicated pool; 72-hour operational watch with daily executive sync at 18:00 ET.

Rollback triggers (examples): p50 latency > 350ms for 15+ minutes, or sustained error rate >1.5% — immediate rollback to hosted variants and incident bridge.

I’ve updated cutover-checklist.xlsx (tab: timeline & gates) and attached to the Drive link in related_links. Connor — can you confirm the terraform snippet and an estimated time to create lanes (we currently estimate 45–60 minutes once infra is available)?

Priyom
Priyom Das
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

From: James Park <james.park@medalehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@medalehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medale — capacity roadmap, cutover window & autoscale guardrails

Thanks all — that timeline looks reasonable. A few final items from the Medale side before we lock Apr 9–11: 
1) Procurement has one small redline in section 4.2 (data retention parity) — they’ll send the redline by EOD today.
2) We want the warm-cache priming to include a 15-minute live validation (p95 latency check) immediately after kernel warmup completes. Please add that to the smoke test steps.
3) Can you confirm expected monthly unit cost delta for the dedicated pool versus the current hosted spend (ballpark is fine for now) so our finance team can prepare the transfer?

If Redwood can confirm 2) and give a ballpark on 3), we’ll sign the MPA and lock the window.

James
James Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Medale Health

Procurement reply (inline redline) expected from procurement@medalehealth.com — we’ll track in the drive doc. Looking forward to the Terraform snippet Connor will share for quick provisioning.
